title: Tenant-priority degradation and stepped trip thresholds with safe model fallbacks
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: We currently have coarse global circuit breakers that trip by service-level error rates. This causes noisy all-or-nothing outages for customers when a dependency or model variant degrades. We need finer-grained, multi-dimensional breakers that allow: per-tenant soft/hard thresholds, per-model and per-dependency breakers, stepped trip behavior (soft degrade -> partial shed -> hard isolation), and safe fallback prioritization (cache, cheaper model, reduce features).

Goals:
- Prevent a single noisy tenant or model from degrading cluster-level SLOs.
- Provide predictable, explainable fallback behavior that preserves safety and minimal functionality.
- Integrate with multi-region failover: region-aware trip propagation and non-sticky global fallbacks.

Proposal summary:
1) Breaker hierarchy: three orthogonal keys: tenant_id, model_id, dependency_tag. Each request evaluates breakers in this order: tenant -> model -> dependency -> global. Breaker state is computed as max(trip scores) across these keys.
2) Stepped trip thresholds: define three thresholds per breaker: soft(eg 60% degraded), partial(eg 80%), hard(eg 95%). Soft trips enable lightweight degradations (reduce streaming, lower concurrency); partial triggers probabilistic load shedding or route sampling to cheaper model variant; hard trips quarantine traffic (route to fallback pool or return explicit graceful error).
3) Trip scoring: combine multiple signals into a single floating "trip_score" 0..1: 7d-error-rate, p95 latency over target, qps spikes relative to baseline, recent resource saturation (GPU mem/CPU), and explicit operator override. We tune weights per signal per breaker scope. Thresholds map to score bands.
4) Decay and hysteresis: after a trip, score decays with a configurable half-life (default 10m) and requires stability windows to clear. Prevent flapping with minimum open window and exponential backoff for repeated trips.
5) Multi-region behavior: breakers are region-local by default. When a region-level hard trip is observed for a tenant/model, propagate a condensed advisory to other regions that causes them to tighten thresholds for that tenant for a short period rather than instantly quarantining globally. This avoids cascading cross-region failures.
6) Safe fallback hierarchy: (a) prefix/KV cache hit -> respond with cached prediction (tag response as cached), (b) non-streaming single-shot -> fallback to lower-capacity/quantized model within same family, (c) cross-model fallback -> route to a functionally compatible but older model, (d) degrade features -> disable optional tools (context expansion, tool-calls), (e) explicit graceful error with user-friendly payload (include mitigation ETA). Each fallback step has an SLA budget and telemetry.
7) Telemetry & SLO mapping: SLOs include availability (successful responses within latency SLO) per-tenant and per-region. Each breaker action increments budgeted degradation counters and tags traces with breaker scope and reason. Dashboards show per-tenant budget consumption and expected remaining ETA to recovery.
8) Controls & RBAC: Operators can set tenant-priority (critical, normal, experimental). Critical tenants have higher hard-thresholds and wider budgets. Experimental tenants may be subject to lower partial thresholds. RBAC ensures only SREs can set global overrides.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Runtime exposes per-tenant, per-model, per-dependency breaker state and trip_score via admin API and traces.
- When model backend p95 latency doubles, affected model breaker moves to partial state and ~30% of traffic is probabilistically routed to the configured cheaper variant within 2 minutes.
- For a simulated GPU OOM spike, tenant soft->partial->hard sequences follow configured hysteresis and do not cause other tenants to exceed their SLOs in the same region in the test harness.
- Multi-region advisory propagation reduces global cascade in chaos tests (runbook metric: global error spikes decreased by >= 60% compared to naive global quarantining).
- Fallback responses include tags and telemetry for attribution and billing adjustments.

Design doc & references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Stepped+Breaker+Design (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4128
- Telemetry dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rel/breaker-budget-dash

Implementation notes:
- Config schema: JSON per-breaker record with scope, weights, thresholds, half_life_seconds, min_open_seconds, priority_bucket. Example: {scope: "tenant:acct_123", weights: {err:0.5,lat:0.3,qps:0.1,rsrc:0.1}, thresholds:{soft:0.6,partial:0.8,hard:0.95}, half_life_seconds:600, min_open_seconds:30}. Stores: use existing runtime configstore with versioned rollout.
- Fast-path: check cached breaker decision in request evcache keyed by (tenant,model,region) for 30s to minimize evaluation cost.
- Rollout: start with opt-in test tenants, then gradual ramp to 10% of production tenants in a canary mode with tight telemetry and automatic rollback on budget burn.

Runbook excerpt (short):
- Detect: alarm when tenant partial->hard within 5m and budget depletion > 50%.
- Mitigate: temporarily increase soft threshold for non-critical tenants in the region, move critical tenants to reserved pool, activate manual fallback pool.
- Postmortem: annotate timeline with trip_score evolution, region advisory logs, and fallback steps taken.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Admin API returns breaker state and trip_score for tenant/model/dependency (string tags and numeric score). 2) Partial trip causes probabilistic routing to fallback variant within 120s in integration tests. 3) Chaos test: region-level hard trips do not push >1 other tenant over SLO in 90% of runs. 4) Dashboards show per-tenant budget and allow automated alerting when budget < 20%.
